title: Surjectivity of the finite θ-graph projection
statement: For a Noetherian scheme X, ideal J, coherent modules F,F′,H and arrows a:F→H, a′:F′→H, assume ker(a′) and coker(a′) are killed by a positive power of J. For θ:F^→F′^ compatible with a,a′ and n≥0, define E=ker(p₂≫q′−p₁≫q≫θ_n) on F×_H F′, where q,q′ are the J^(n+1) quotient maps. The first projection E→F is an epimorphism. Completion and quotients are from [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Tag 0889(1), affine comparison and uniqueness; Tags 05EK and 088A

proof.text: Apply the finite formal-graph first-quotient epimorphism to the prescribed compatible formal map. This gives E→F/JF epi without using either torsion hypothesis.

Choose the exponent s from the given comparison torsion data. Apply the proved kernel-pullback cokernel bound to the graph discrepancy; J^(s+n+1) kills coker(E→F). Only the comparison cokernel hypothesis is needed.

Let C=coker(E→F). Naturality of quotient maps and cancellation of E→F/JF show that C→C/JC is zero. At a stalk, the ideal-power quotient formula gives IC=C and the annihilator formula gives I^(s+n+1)C=0. Induct on k using I^(k+1)C=I^k(IC) to obtain I^kC=C; hence C=0. Section extensionality detects this globally, and the categorical zero-cokernel criterion proves epimorphy.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0889(1), finite-graph comparison reduced to closed-fibre surjectivity and a proved power-annihilator bound; final power-annihilated Nakayama argument as in Algebra Tag 00DV(9).

theorem torsionControlledGraphFst_epi
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    {H F F' : CoherentModules X} (a : F ⟶ H) (a' : F' ⟶ H)
    (ha' : ∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (kernel a'.hom)) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (cokernel a'.hom)))
    (θ : (completion X J).obj F ⟶ (completion X J).obj F')
    (hθ : θ ≫ (completion X J).map a' = (completion X J).map a)
    (n : ℕ) : Epi (torsionControlledGraphFst J a a' θ n)
